Lukhanyiso, Broken Field of Dreams.

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carte Blanche goes into the Free state to investigate farming projects and finds a horrifying picture

Unique Selling Point:
Great case studies and all the documentation to tell our story properly and full access

Summary:
In February 2013 The Lukhanyiso farming project was launched by the Department of Rural Development and land reform in the Free state.

The idea was to create 90 small scale BEE farms, creating 370 jobs with a gross yearly profit of R37.5 million rand. The project was conducted over a period of five years from Feb 2013 to January 2017

In a progress report the projections were as follows:

The gross yearly turnover for each of the 90 pig and chicken farms is around R640,000, while the central farms annual turnover escalates to R21,4 mill in year 3 onwards. The income and expense analysis provide for a profitable gross margin profit business case with a total of R135,9 mill profit over the 5-year period. The operational budget for the Lukhanyiso Farm will be R23 mill annually where 90 BEE farms will be managing 9,000 pigs and 112,500
chickens, or an annual production of 30,938 pigs and 843,750 chickens. The capital budget for the development of the 90 individual farms and the centre farm is around R57 mill.



Further information:
But like all these projects under the auspices of the Department of Rural Development and land reform the community farmers were given a strategic partner. The first man was a Danish project manager called Carsten Laugesen from the LTE and EBF group.
his achievements are listed as follows:

Laugesen was for three years development counsellor at the Royal Danish Embassy, South Africa, responsible for the R1,5 billion development and financial energy and environmental cooperation between Denmark and Southern Africa. Before that he worked for 12 years in one of Europe’s largest engineering consulting companies, COWI, as head of department and project manager for technical capacity development and installation projects around the world. Involved in the design, appraisal, implementation and evaluation of more than 80 international projects during the last twenty years, Mr Laugesen has acquired a comprehensive knowledge of project management and methods for innovation, implementation, problem analysis, surveying, bench marking and evaluation. He has worked repeatedly for the same clients within EU, Danida, Danced. Before his present CEO of EBF Group position, , World Bank, Ministries, Counties and Local Governments, particular in South Africa, Denmark, Europe and South East Asia. Mr. Laugesen is the author and co-author of 19 books, 117 technical reports and 20 articles. He has lectured on many different subjects such as renewable energy financing, IPP structuring, energy and environmental regulations.

The second strategic partner is a man called Malisela Manaka. He spent just under 15 years working in the Agricultural and Rural Development sector, where he grew from the bottom up. His responsibilities included project management, community facilitation, agricultural business planning and business plan assessments for Government funded projects. It also included program management across the entire Gauteng province. As a Director of Land Reform in the Gauteng Province, Mr Manaka was responsible for the implementation of the Government ‘s Land Reform Program in the province. This included the establishment of the small, medium and commercial black farmers. He was as well responsible for the stakeholder relations and management, human and financial resources management. He was responsible for a budget of about R200m in a financial year and in excess of R 500m over a three year Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) Government financial
planning period. Mr Manaka was the appointed as the Acting Chief Director for the Gauteng Province in control of the entire Rural Development and Land Reform Department’s programs. This position placed him at the highest level of interaction in the Department and the province both administratively and politically. Mr Manaka is partner in Innovate Farming Systems and furthermore Chief Executive Officer of Projects et al Holdings (Pty) Ltd, a company that offers accredited SETA based training, Agricultural Enterprise Development and Consulting Services

But here comes the story- five years later over R137 million rand has been spent on this project – there is nothing much on the land except a huge bio digester that doesn’t work
And the people are furious that they have been ripped off. And who has ripped them off – well let us ask this question: “Why has Laugeson got a R13 million rand bond on his Houghton home in Johannesburg. Why have all the so called projects been funnelled through companies owned by the strategic partners.

Carte Blanche reveals how a community of rural dwellers have had their dreams shattered and NO ONE in government has done anything to stem what is clearly stealing from the poor.

Press Release:


Lukhanyiso: A Field of Broken Dreams
Carte Blanche investigates the Lukhanyiso Food and Energy Centre in the Free State, which promised emerging farmers a shot at a sustainable future in agriculture and alternative power. Let down by their strategic partner and the Department of Rural Development and Land Reform, the project has been at a standstill, with little to show for the millions of Rands invested. But that didn’t stop the Development Bank of Southern Africa from investing another R60 million in a bio-digester that’s now a white elephant. We ask what went wrong with this flagship project.
Producer: Joy Summers
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender
Researcher: Laura Byrne


Script:


Lukhanyiso -Field of broken dreams Final script TX SUNDAY 17TH MARCH 2019

Commentary One
In 2013, 90 Free State families formed a co-operative farm from 2800 hectares of land they had been given by the state. They divided the farm into 90 plots and called it Lukhanyiso

LINK
On each plot was supposed to be one small caretaker house and either a chicken house or a small piggery.

Commentary Two
Free State Rural Development allocated R54 million rand to build these structures and bring in the livestock, and Justina Mabekebeke became the first chairperson of the committee.
This photograph in her small sitting room reminds her of a time filled with hope

Justina
That man whose taking that photograph he was coming from Denmark

Commentary Three
6 years later the project has left her heartbroken

Devi
Because in the end is that what happened. No?
Justina Mabekebeke
Eh nothing. It’s only these pictures which we are having

Commentary Four
The project was led by a strategic partner, a jet-setting Dane, Mr. Carsten Laugesen.
He devised an ambitious business plan and signed a five- year contract with the department, to mentor the farmers towards prosperity.

Devi link
Well R54 million rand later, and I simply cannot see where the money has gone

Commentary five
By now you should be seeing 360 hectares of crops, 45 piggeries, 45 chicken houses, 90 little homes, 112 000 chickens, 9 000 pigs, a central farm with a breeding station, a 5MW solar farm, and a small bio digester which would provide free electricity using the pig and chicken manure as fuel.

Devi
Where are the rest of the people?
Jomo Radebe
Down at the location. They are stranded. They are angry



Commentary six
Jomo Radebe was the chairperson of the committee that took over from Justina. Only 20 out of 90 plots were completed, and he says Carsten Laugesen let them down.

Jomo
Mr. Carsten Laugesen, he is the person who can clarify what happened to the money?
Devi
So, when you asked him questions about the money, what would he say?
Jomo
He would get angry. When you question him, question the truth he will tell you, you are nothing, you cannot come and tell me that, because I am the person who is looking after everything here

Commentary seven
Zolile Manqthu’s father was a committee member in 2013. Back then Zolile was concerned
his father didn’t understand what he was signing. He was also alarmed by the large sums being transferred to Laugesens private companies

Devi
Did you read what you are signing
Justina
You know as you are coming to us now
Devi
In a rush
Justina
Rush and tell me that…
Devi
Sign, sign, sign!
Then we trust you as we have been given you by the government to come and assist us, we trust that you are doing the good things
Devi
How do you feel now?
Justina
I want him to pay
Devi
Because there is nothing there
Justina
I am sick now ….when I remember this my heart …she gets emotional
Devi
Are you saying to me, that Mr. Laugesen lied to you?
Justina
He lied to us…
Devi
And out of trust you signed things, but do you understand now what you signed.
Justina
Yes. Yes. I understand now that we just signed for Carsten to eat our money

Commentary eight
Repeatedly we asked Laugesen for an interview. We wrote to him. We called him

Ring, ring…

We went to his company EBF, but it has moved. This week we called again

Devi
Hello Mr. Laugesen, its Devi from Carte Blanche, how are you?
I am ok, thank you
I have been trying to get hold of you for a while …

Commentary nine
We wanted details of how the money had been spent. But all Laugesen would say was that he was just a simple consultant and we should speak to the department.

Laugesen
I am a simple consultant
Devi
Yes, but you were the strategic partner on the project

Commentary ten
Then he hung up.

Beep… beep….

In a written response Laugesen denies he benefitted from the funding and says each payment was authorized by the beneficiaries and verified by the department. He says he never lied to the community and he is still trying to help them

Devi
Do you believe Carsten Laugesen was funneling the money to his own companies?
Zolile
Yes.
Devi
There is no doubt in your mind about that
Zolile
There is no doubt

Commentary eleven
Laugesen was the CEO and one of the directors of the strategic partner, LTE Farming.
Two of his companies Innovate Building and Innovate Farming systems received money from this project

LINK
You don’t have to be a forensic auditor to see what has happened here. These documents show how people who trusted, have been taken advantage of

Commentary twelve
The bank accounts confirm that the first Rural Development tranche of R25 million came into the account in Feb 2013, and just five invoices from Laugesens various companies burnt through the entire first tranche of R25 million within three months.

LINK
The alarm bells that something was wrong were already ringing in late 2013 as this document shows, but that didn’t make the slightest bit of difference

Commentary thirteen
Laugesen says he has complied with Rural and land reform regulations, but the departments own external audit firm, questioned his financial governance, deviations from budgeted spending and vague invoices.

Zolile
This is exploitation to our people

Commentary fourteen
The auditors recommended that urgent action needed to be taken to get the committee members more involved in what was happening to their recap funds.

Click. Click farmer photoshop.

But as long as it all looked good, who cared? Laugesen brought in his Copenhagen photographer. The people brought their animals

CLICK!
Four committees have tried to save the project. LMJ Phume was the third chairperson

LMJ Phume
Let me tell you it’s the departments fault. Because the people who donated the funds are the department, and the department is the one who has to monitor the funds

Commentary fifteen
But the department refuted the allegations and insisted they had monitored the project throughout and had not released funds without addressing the concerns raised by the auditors.

Devi
What profits was the farm supposed to be making now
Zolile
In the fifth year the total amount was R147 54 163
Devi
And what is the farm generating now?
Zolile
Nothing

Commentary sixteen
The final R6 million didn’t save the project and by 2017 Lukhanyiso was at a standstill.

MUSIC UPSOUND OVER BIODIGESTER

But Laugesen wasn’t done yet. He then raised another R60 million. This time from the Development bank. Apart from his role as mentor he now became a 40% shareholder in this bio digester, in partnership with the 90 families he had let down once already.

Zolile Manqthu
if Carsten Laugesen is going to get 40% from those digesters – that means that in each million he will get R400 000 and these poor families will share R600 000 that means 90 families will get R6666 each and they have to pay back the money which is a loan from DBSA so Ma’am this is really devastating!

Commentary seventeen
At 5 MW Its 25 times larger than the one Laugesen had originally proposed

LINK
but is it ever going to work, because even at the time it was built it needed thousands of tonnes of feedstock to create energy, and where is that going to come from?

Commentary eighteen
Jomo Radebe once championed the Bio digester project

Devi
So how do you feel about the fact that you were part of the committee that gave him permission to do this, that you spoke to the DBSA, its built here and its doing nothing?
Jomo
Ma’am I am so ashamed. I felt so betrayed. It feels as if I failed my people.

Devi
You are a former policeman, how did you fall for this?
Jomo
Corruption ma’am. If people can investigate this thing, there are many things I know I can assist in that

Commentary nineteen
Curiously no provision was made back in 2017 to provide the 64 000 tonnes of feedstock it needs to run.
Devi
Did you guys not wonder where was the feedstock coming from because there were no pigs no chickens
Jomo
I was asking that question every day for Mr. Laugeson. He used to say I am on that I know about that thing

Commentary twenty
We were perplexed why the Development Bank would give the strategic partner with such a lousy track record on the first project, yet another R60 million rand. After all, over R100 million has already been spent at Lukhanyiso and neither the farm or the digester work.

Olympus Manthata is head of Climate finance

Devi
So, we are seven years down the line now what do we have to show for it?
Olympus
We are coming in to introduce a component to the project that we believe can add value
Devi
So, you don’t blame me for thinking this is a con?
Olympus
I have confidence in the plans we have put in place to return the project back on track

Commentary twenty-one
The Bank say they have done their due diligence, and the upliftment of the 90 farmers is imperative. They also say the farmers won’t lose their land to pay off the loan

Devi to Olympus
In any country anywhere, you will not get money to do a project, mess it up and then another institution related to the state will give you more money to fix that project up that you messed up, and then this one has a problem and we give you more money to fix it up, …that is what this is
Olympus
I think you determine where you have challenges to the project, what is the best way forward, whether you let it go
Devi
Or you change out the strategic partner? You change out the person who seems to be the problem from the beginning
Olympus
If you have information before you…
Devi
if I can get this information, I don’t know why you don’t have it
Olympus
We can show you information of the work we have done
Devi
Do you know how I expected you to react? I expected you to say Devi this is shocking, I agree with you there is nothing there we have been there/ the farmers are unhappy I expected you to say that instead is all you are saying to me I am going to stick to our processes and if this is what we have that is our processes, cos what I am hearing is a passing of the buck
Olympus
I think the intention is not to pass the buck … any new information that comes through to us obviously we will look at that
Devi
You should have known this before
Olympus
That is why I am responding to you the processes that we have followed
Devi
No. It’s shocking you didn’t pick it up!

Commentary twenty- two
Laugesen has convinced the bank that he can get the digester working by November, by paying the next- door farmer R16 000 per hectare to grow and deliver grass. Except they haven’t planted the grass yet, and winter is coming. Laugesen is offering the Lukhanyiso farmers only R300 per hectare to lease their land.

Devi
When is the bio digester going to start working?
Olympus
the idea is that we should start to see the flow of gas end November beginning December

Commentary twenty- three
The bank believes they can still save the project and use the profits from the Bio digester to build up the farm. We hope they are right, or Justina Mbekebeke and her old committee may never see the better life they were once promised by Rural Development and Carsten Laugesen.

THE END 12 mins 06

PROMO ONE
90 land reform beneficiaries have lost faith in their strategic partner, who was supposed to mentor them towards prosperity
Zolile
This is exploitation of our people

PROMO TWO
Over R100 million rand spent by government on a Free State farm with very little to show for it
Devi
Where are the rest of the people?
Jomo Radebe
Down at the location. They are stranded. They are angry

PROMO THREE
We follow the money of a communal Free State farm project to see why it failed.
Devi
Hello Mr. Laugesen, its Devi from Carte Blanche, how are you?
I am ok, thank you


NAMES OF PARTICIPANTS

JUSTINA MABEKEBEKE
FORMER CHAIRPERSON: LUKHANYISO 1st COMMITTEE

JOMO RADEBE
FORMER CHAIRPERSON: LUKHANYISO 2nd COMMITTEE

ZOLILE MANQUTHU
CHAIRPERSON 4TH COMMITTEE: LUKHANYISO

LMJ PHUME
CHAIRPERSON 3RD COMMITTEE: LUKHANYISO

OLYMPUS MANTHATA
HEAD: CLIMATE FINANCE DBSA

I am ok, thank you I have been trying to get hold of you for a while … Commentary nine We wanted details of how the money had been spent. But all Laugesen would say was that he was just a simple consultant and we should speak to the department. Laugesen I am a simple consultant Devi Yes, but you were the strategic partner on the project Commentary ten Then he hung up. Beep… beep…. In a written response Laugesen denies he benefitted from the funding and says each payment was authorized by the beneficiaries and verified by the department. He says he never lied to the community and he is still trying to help them Devi Do you believe Carsten Laugesen was funneling the money to his own companies? Zolile Yes. Devi There is no doubt in your mind about that Zolile There is no doubt Commentary eleven Laugesen was the CEO and one of the directors of the strategic partner, LTE Farming. Two of his companies Innovate Building and Innovate Farming systems received money from this project LINK You don’t have to be a forensic auditor to see what has happened here. These documents show how people who trusted, have been taken advantage of Commentary twelve The bank accounts confirm that the first Rural Development tranche of R25 million came into the account in Feb 2013, and just five invoices from Laugesens various companies burnt through the entire first tranche of R25 million within three months. LINK The alarm bells that something was wrong were already ringing in late 2013 as this document shows, but that didn’t make the slightest bit of difference Commentary thirteen Laugesen says he has complied with Rural and land reform regulations, but the departments own external audit firm, questioned his financial governance, deviations from budgeted spending and vague invoices. Zolile This is exploitation to our people Commentary fourteen The auditors recommended that urgent action needed to be taken to get the committee members more involved in what was happening to their recap funds. Click. Click farmer photoshop. But as long as it all looked good, who cared? Laugesen brought in his Copenhagen photographer. The people brought their animals CLICK! Four committees have tried to save the project. LMJ Phume was the third chairperson LMJ Phume Let me tell you it’s the departments fault. Because the people who donated the funds are the department, and the department is the one who has to monitor the funds Commentary fifteen But the department refuted the allegations and insisted they had monitored the project throughout and had not released funds without addressing the concerns raised by the auditors. Devi What profits was the farm supposed to be making now Zolile In the fifth year the total amount was R147 54 163 Devi And what is the farm generating now? Zolile Nothing Commentary sixteen The final R6 million didn’t save the project and by 2017 Lukhanyiso was at a standstill. MUSIC UPSOUND OVER BIODIGESTER But Laugesen wasn’t done yet. He then raised another R60 million. This time from the Development bank. Apart from his role as mentor he now became a 40% shareholder in this bio digester, in partnership with the 90 families he had let down once already. Zolile Manqthu if Carsten Laugesen is going to get 40% from those digesters – that means that in each million he will get R400 000 and these poor families will share R600 000 that means 90 families will get R6666 each and they have to pay back the money which is a loan from DBSA so Ma’am this is really devastating! Commentary seventeen At 5 MW Its 25 times larger than the one Laugesen had originally proposed LINK but is it ever going to work, because even at the time it was built it needed thousands of tonnes of feedstock to create energy, and where is that going to come from? Commentary eighteen Jomo Radebe once championed the Bio digester project Devi So how do you feel about the fact that you were part of the committee that gave him permission to do this, that you spoke to the DBSA, its built here and its doing nothing? Jomo Ma’am I am so ashamed. I felt so betrayed. It feels as if I failed my people. Devi You are a former policeman, how did you fall for this? Jomo Corruption ma’am. If people can investigate this thing, there are many things I know I can assist in that Commentary nineteen Curiously no provision was made back in 2017 to provide the 64 000 tonnes of feedstock it needs to run. Devi Did you guys not wonder where was the feedstock coming from because there were no pigs no chickens Jomo I was asking that question every day for Mr. Laugeson. He used to say I am on that I know about that thing Commentary twenty We were perplexed why the Development Bank would give the strategic partner with such a lousy track record on the first project, yet another R60 million rand. After all, over R100 million has already been spent at Lukhanyiso and neither the farm or the digester work. Olympus Manthata is head of Climate finance Devi So, we are seven years down the line now what do we have to show for it? Olympus We are coming in to introduce a component to the project that we believe can add value Devi So, you don’t blame me for thinking this is a con? Olympus I have confidence in the plans we have put in place to return the project back on track Commentary twenty-one The Bank say they have done their due diligence, and the upliftment of the 90 farmers is imperative. They also say the farmers won’t lose their land to pay off the loan Devi to Olympus In any country anywhere, you will not get money to do a project, mess it up and then another institution related to the state will give you more money to fix that project up that you messed up, and then this one has a problem and we give you more money to fix it up, …that is what this is Olympus I think you determine where you have challenges to the project, what is the best way forward, whether you let it go Devi Or you change out the strategic partner? You change out the person who seems to be the problem from the beginning Olympus If you have information before you… Devi if I can get this information, I don’t know why you don’t have it Olympus We can show you information of the work we have done Devi Do you know how I expected you to react? I expected you to say Devi this is shocking, I agree with you there is nothing there we have been there/ the farmers are unhappy I expected you to say that instead is all you are saying to me I am going to stick to our processes and if this is what we have that is our processes, cos what I am hearing is a passing of the buck Olympus I think the intention is not to pass the buck … any new information that comes through to us obviously we will look at that Devi You should have known this before Olympus That is why I am responding to you the processes that we have followed Devi No. It’s shocking you didn’t pick it up! Commentary twenty- two Laugesen has convinced the bank that he can get the digester working by November, by paying the next- door farmer R16 000 per hectare to grow and deliver grass. Except they haven’t planted the grass yet, and winter is coming. Laugesen is offering the Lukhanyiso farmers only R300 per hectare to lease their land. Devi When is the bio digester going to start working? Olympus the idea is that we should start to see the flow of gas end November beginning December Commentary twenty- three The bank believes they can still save the project and use the profits from the Bio digester to build up the farm. We hope they are right, or Justina Mbekebeke and her old committee may never see the better life they were once promised by Rural Development and Carsten Laugesen. THE END 12 mins 06 PROMO ONE 90 land reform beneficiaries have lost faith in their strategic partner, who was supposed to mentor them towards prosperity Zolile This is exploitation of our people PROMO TWO Over R100 million rand spent by government on a Free State farm with very little to show for it Devi Where are the rest of the people? Jomo Radebe Down at the location. They are stranded. They are angry PROMO THREE We follow the money of a communal Free State farm project to see why it failed. Devi Hello Mr. Laugesen, its Devi from Carte Blanche, how are you? I am ok, thank you NAMES OF PARTICIPANTS JUSTINA MABEKEBEKE FORMER CHAIRPERSON: LUKHANYISO 1st COMMITTEE JOMO RADEBE FORMER CHAIRPERSON: LUKHANYISO 2nd COMMITTEE ZOLILE MANQUTHU CHAIRPERSON 4TH COMMITTEE: LUKHANYISO LMJ PHUME CHAIRPERSON 3RD COMMITTEE: LUKHANYISO OLYMPUS MANTHATA HEAD: CLIMATE FINANCE DBSA Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Lukhanyiso, Broken Field of Dreams. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Carte Blanche goes into the Free state to investigate farming projects and finds a horrifying picture
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Great case studies and all the documentation to tell our story properly and full access
metadata.Summary: In February 2013 The Lukhanyiso farming project was launched by the Department of Rural Development and land reform in the Free state. The idea was to create 90 small scale BEE farms, creating 370 jobs with a gross yearly profit of R37.5 million rand. The project was conducted over a period of five years from Feb 2013 to January 2017 In a progress report the projections were as follows: The gross yearly turnover for each of the 90 pig and chicken farms is around R640,000, while the central farms annual turnover escalates to R21,4 mill in year 3 onwards. The income and expense analysis provide for a profitable gross margin profit business case with a total of R135,9 mill profit over the 5-year period. The operational budget for the Lukhanyiso Farm will be R23 mill annually where 90 BEE farms will be managing 9,000 pigs and 112,500 chickens, or an annual production of 30,938 pigs and 843,750 chickens. The capital budget for the development of the 90 individual farms and the centre farm is around R57 mill.
metadata.Further information: But like all these projects under the auspices of the Department of Rural Development and land reform the community farmers were given a strategic partner. The first man was a Danish project manager called Carsten Laugesen from the LTE and EBF group. his achievements are listed as follows: Laugesen was for three years development counsellor at the Royal Danish Embassy, South Africa, responsible for the R1,5 billion development and financial energy and environmental cooperation between Denmark and Southern Africa. Before that he worked for 12 years in one of Europe’s largest engineering consulting companies, COWI, as head of department and project manager for technical capacity development and installation projects around the world. Involved in the design, appraisal, implementation and evaluation of more than 80 international projects during the last twenty years, Mr Laugesen has acquired a comprehensive knowledge of project management and methods for innovation, implementation, problem analysis, surveying, bench marking and evaluation. He has worked repeatedly for the same clients within EU, Danida, Danced. Before his present CEO of EBF Group position, , World Bank, Ministries, Counties and Local Governments, particular in South Africa, Denmark, Europe and South East Asia. Mr. Laugesen is the author and co-author of 19 books, 117 technical reports and 20 articles. He has lectured on many different subjects such as renewable energy financing, IPP structuring, energy and environmental regulations. The second strategic partner is a man called Malisela Manaka. He spent just under 15 years working in the Agricultural and Rural Development sector, where he grew from the bottom up. His responsibilities included project management, community facilitation, agricultural business planning and business plan assessments for Government funded projects. It also included program management across the entire Gauteng province. As a Director of Land Reform in the Gauteng Province, Mr Manaka was responsible for the implementation of the Government ‘s Land Reform Program in the province. This included the establishment of the small, medium and commercial black farmers. He was as well responsible for the stakeholder relations and management, human and financial resources management. He was responsible for a budget of about R200m in a financial year and in excess of R 500m over a three year Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) Government financial planning period. Mr Manaka was the appointed as the Acting Chief Director for the Gauteng Province in control of the entire Rural Development and Land Reform Department’s programs. This position placed him at the highest level of interaction in the Department and the province both administratively and politically. Mr Manaka is partner in Innovate Farming Systems and furthermore Chief Executive Officer of Projects et al Holdings (Pty) Ltd, a company that offers accredited SETA based training, Agricultural Enterprise Development and Consulting Services But here comes the story- five years later over R137 million rand has been spent on this project – there is nothing much on the land except a huge bio digester that doesn’t work And the people are furious that they have been ripped off. And who has ripped them off – well let us ask this question: “Why has Laugeson got a R13 million rand bond on his Houghton home in Johannesburg. Why have all the so called projects been funnelled through companies owned by the strategic partners. Carte Blanche reveals how a community of rural dwellers have had their dreams shattered and NO ONE in government has done anything to stem what is clearly stealing from the poor.
